items.title: Define the trusted-execution policy, closed schema, and fail-closed backend contract
items.notes: Merged PR #9178. The process-free policy core provides closed execution records, immutable corpus and adapter identities, explicit operator authorization, and a backend interface that cannot fall back to host execution. This item does not execute fixture code.

items.title: Define the Linux OCI identity, capability preflight, and invariant-probe container
items.notes: Merged PR #9189. The closed identity binds rootless Podman, crun, exact OCI manifest/config, seccomp, shim, and probe; the original module defined fail-closed host/image preflight and exact probe-container argv without fixture decode or launch. The current broker tranche leaves that backend process-free. The checked-in policy remains disabled and Linux unavailable until protected enforcement evidence exists.

items.title: Define the external authority bundle and Linux preflight profile
items.notes: Merged PR #9196. Security review split out a safe first profile: a post-merge external bundle whose raw-byte approval binds the exact source commit/tree, policy, schemas, authority verifier, Linux preflight backend, and external backend identity. Schema v1 approves exact bytes for capability inspection only, with no corpus, adapter, container, executable payload, or process handoff. Validation covered 108 focused tests, 86% branch-aware authority-module coverage, Ruff, Bandit, corpus/contract validators, Go tests/build, parity collision checks, and the unchanged 73-gap build-file audit.

items.title: Load the exact approved preflight backend through an atomic runner boundary
items.notes: Merged PR #9208. The domain-separated ten-role loader authority binds exact approved verifier, loader, backend, manifest, identity, policy, and schema bytes; retained no-follow directory handles and sealed memfds close component races. The isolated worker validates an exact stdlib import closure and closed interfaces by AST plus compilation without importing the backend or running Podman. Validation covered 125 conformance tests, 67% combined branch-aware coverage, Ruff, Bandit, corpus/contract validators, Go tests/build, parity collision checks, and the unchanged 73-gap build-file audit. Linux-only filesystem, sealed-worker, process-group, and streaming-cap paths passed Ubuntu CI.

items.title: Broker the two approved Linux OCI capability commands
items.notes: Merged PR #9231. The separately domain-bound broker verifies statically linked amd64 Podman plus crun and Conmon, rejects malformed ELF and PT_INTERP, FD-executes only retained Podman bytes for forced-local version and exact-config image inspection, confines pathname-backed execution with a mandatory Landlock ruleset whose sole allow-rule is the retained Podman inode, keeps its worker protocol non-authoritative and source-free, bounds combined output, scrubs environment/descriptors, and owns timeout plus delegated-cgroup descendant kill/reap. It creates no container, fixture, adapter, or invariant probe; anonymous executable memfds and executable mappings remain separately gated.

items.title: Bind execution to the exact approved in-memory case snapshot
items.notes: Discovered during the Linux OCI security review. Select the requested direct corpus member from one root-handle/no-follow bounded snapshot and execute the same hashed bytes; reject outside paths, renames, symlinks, hardlinks, case/Unicode aliases, and post-digest mutation.

items.title: Bind protected Linux execution to an immutable runner-image TCB receipt
items.notes: Discovered during the capability-broker security review. Capability preflight validates a static Podman ELF and FD-executes it under Landlock, which permits pathname-backed execution only of that retained inode and denies constructor hooks, pause helpers, dynamic-loader trampolines, and other pathname-backed helpers in the reviewed flow; it separately verifies crun and Conmon without executing them. Future container execution still makes their absolute paths, the protected Python interpreter, stdlib/native extensions, libc, loaders for later runtime components, container configuration defaults, and remaining immutable host dependencies runner-image obligations that require a verifiable out-of-band attestation before protected evidence can authorize an invariant probe.

items.title: Close anonymous executable and executable-mapping paths
items.notes: Merged PR #9270. The exact broker behavior closes unlisted descriptors before its final sandbox transition, starts retained Podman through pathname execve under the exact-inode Landlock rule, and installs inherited amd64 classic-seccomp enforcement that kills architecture/x32 bypasses and denies execveat, new anonymous executable files, executable mappings, descriptor receipt or acquisition, SHM_EXEC, uselib, and io_uring surfaces. Linux integration probes cover the real close-before-sandbox sequence, retained-inode execution, foreign and anonymous FD denial, executable mmap/mprotect/pkey_mprotect, fresh-inode dlopen, descendant inheritance, and stable install failure. It creates no container, fixture, adapter, invariant probe, or readiness receipt.

items.title: Normalize dependency-skip terminology and result-state invariants
items.notes: Discovered during the fixture audit. Replace the duplicated schema term dependency-skipped with normative dep-skipped and enforce built, failed, dep-skipped, would-build, return-code, command-state, and outcome consistency before execution cases enter the corpus.

It binds no execution case or adapter.

items.title: Run and police the Linux OCI invariant probe
items.notes: Execute only after exact-byte loading and invariant-probe authority. Add aggregate cgroup CPU metering, combined streaming output/result accounting, hard workspace semantics, cancellation, whole-container kill/reap/removal, adversarial runner-owned probes, and protected Linux workflow evidence before marking Linux ready. This item runs no fixture case.

Preflight and invariant-probe approvals remain structurally unusable for a fixture case.

items.notes: Require a capability-less AppContainer or LPAC, private DACLs, root-handle reparse-safe filesystem operations, and a Job Object assigned before resume with no breakaway and whole-tree CPU, memory, process, wall, output, and workspace limits.

items.notes: Fail closed until a signed sandbox helper or isolated VM backend can enforce filesystem and network denial plus aggregate process-tree CPU, memory, process, wall, output, workspace, and termination limits. sandbox-exec alone is not sufficient evidence.
